research_contract.question: When should a strong project owner work directly or delegate bounded tasks to improve accepted outcomes per unit of time, attention and compute?
source_scopes: Publication-safe task, dispatch, review and recovery receipts
Paired or naturally occurring work with explicit acceptance criteria
research_contract.decision_to_change: Choose direct work, bounded delegation or a stronger owner for a defined task class after accounting for setup, review and repair.
success_criteria: Compare accepted outcomes for the same task class and include preparation, verification and repair costs.
Keep route compatibility, task quality and account cost as separate observations.
falsifiers: The apparent delegation gain disappears after verification and repair are counted.
A cheaper or faster method produces more rejected outcomes or loses the intended task.
evidence_gaps: No public controlled result establishes a universal model, delegation or cost multiplier.
watch_triggers: New owner-approved outcome or counterexample changes the decision evidence.
The relevant source, operating constraint or acceptance boundary materially changes.
research_contract.answer_shape: A task-class decision table with the baseline, accepted result, full effort/cost accounting, counterexamples and uncertainty.
research_contract.refresh_policy: Review when relevant owner evidence or decision conditions change; registration starts no collector, benchmark, scheduler or new execution lane.
research_contract.state_note: Library-authored proposed criteria and counterevidence, not an evaluated method or accepted answer. This metadata does not establish measured gains, commercial commitments or authorization for new execution.
